before_snapshot.source: Arvidsson and Molander 2017, DOI10.1111/jiec.12526; Warren et al.2015, DOI10.1021/acs.est.5b01627. Published PVT substrate reference.
before_snapshot.comment:
CONSISTENT SiC WAFER/FABRICATION BASIS, 2026-10-20. This supersedes the earlier4kWh/cm2-physical-wafer and35%yield interpretation. Warren2015 https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.5b01627 primary manuscript section4.1 https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/1855705 defines4.04kWh/cm2 of FUNCTIONAL DIE, including perimeter/nonfunctional die losses. Its100mm reference has81.07cm2/wafer,1314gooddies*3.42mm2=44.9388cm2goodarea; thus2.239456667kWh/cm2physical usable wafer. Its6.6cm boule yields47good350um wafers after kerf/polishing and bad wafers; retained wafer/boule mass=47*.035/6.6=0.2492424242. This is a published reference design, not current measured factory yield. Net consumed Acheson SiC powder is represented as the boule mass,100%net conversion; actual PVT-grade purification/charge losses remain unrepresented. Unused circulating charge is not repeatedly purchased. The wafer provider output remains1kg PHYSICAL350um wafer, not1kg of good chips. Supply its net discarded crystal/kerf once to the existing mineral waste proxy. No argon amount or direct-growth emissions is established. Spejo2023 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pedc.2023.100050 Table1/section3 models150mm SiC MOSFET processing with520potential25mm2dies and442gooddies (85%electrical yield). These are future-maturity estimates and a3.3kV source analogue, not measured650/1200/2300V part production. Selected scenario3 front-end electricity4.99kWh/cm2GOODDIE already includes wafer utilization/yield; do NOT divide it again by0.85. Test its four published scenarios 2.50,3.01,4.99,6.02kWh/cm2. Source good-area fraction=442*.25/(pi*7.5^2)=0.62530; physical wafer input/good-die area=1/that fraction. Finished SiC mass is held fixed. Infer delivered die area from3210kg/m3 and350um unthinned-die reference, not a measured thickness; test175/100um. Thinning and cutting reject mass=physical wafer input minus retained SiC, treated once separately from upstream crystal/kerf. Failed dies are assumed bare SiC in this nominal ledger; discarded metallization and process chemicals remain unquantified. The electrical good-die yield is separate from geometry and wafer-growth losses. Linear wafer-area transfer from Warren substrate to Spejo geometry is explicit: total substrate electricity is recalculated on physical wafer area, not copied from already-yield-adjusted4.04 a second time. Add front-end electricity to any EXISTING package-assembly allowance; do not add substrate electricity again in device helpers or charge a second packaged transistor. Global electricity remains a geography proxy. No operating electricity, device counts, retained package metals/masses, voltage identities, final equipment EOL or lifetime coefficients change. This closes known electricity and nominal reject boundaries only: SiC epitaxy/etch/deposition/doping chemicals, process gas utilization/abatement, direct emissions, actual chip geometry, module packaging and industrial qualification remain open. An energy range is not evidence for toxicity completeness. No fabricated gas capture or extra silicon/DRAM chemical recipe. All parameters are static references, not a newly inferred time-learning curve. Only existing supplemental workbooks change; no runtime/YAML/native edits.
PREVIOUS NOTES (retained as history; the correction above takes precedence):
SiC SUBSTRATE MANUFACTURE, 2026-10-19. Arvidsson and Molander (2017), DOI 10.1111/jiec.12526, section Silicon Carbide Wafer Production / Physical Vapor Transport, citing Warren et al. (2015), DOI 10.1021/acs.est.5b01627: PVT substrate electricity 4.0 kWh/cm2 for a 350 micrometre wafer, density 3210 kg/m3, net wafer-material yield 0.35 including poor crystal regions, slicing and polishing. Thus per kg finished wafer: electricity 35603.0262572 kWh and Acheson SiC powder 1/0.35 = 2.85714285714 kg. Source linearly scales growth electricity with thickness; this mass-normalized reference uses its 350 micrometre basis. Unused charge recirculates internally and is not purchased again; the net discarded 1/0.35-1 kg SiC goes once to generic inert-waste disposal, with no recovery credit. This waste fate is an explicit proxy for discarded crystal/kerf. The source omits measured argon and direct growth emissions; those are unresolved, not demonstrated zero. Global electricity is a geographic proxy. This restores SUBSTRATE production instead of buying industrial SiC powder as a finished semiconductor. It does NOT include device epitaxy, lithography, implantation, metallization, die yields or package assembly. Those remain separate open boundaries; do not interpret this as a complete SiC transistor LCI or a current vendor-specific process. Retain declared finished SiC die mass, package metals/resins, part counts, service life, operating losses and EOL. Do not purchase a complete packaged power device on top. Published reference is historical: test electricity 2/4/6 kWh/cm2 and wafer yield 0.35/0.50/0.70 as illustrative process sensitivities, not measured statistics. Source https://link.springer.com/article/10.1111/jiec.12526 (CC BY 4.0); full text https://publications.lib.chalmers.se/records/fulltext/253433/local_253433.pdf . Only existing supplemental workbooks change; no runtime, native, mapping or primary/secondary-share edits.
